notes: §1985:XVI.1.4.3 GRL2.2 puts an independent segment in its last-used state when "Control is transferred explicitly to that segment as the result of the execution of an EXIT PROGRAM statement". At --std 85 the segment-number is admitted (VersionConformancePass.VisitSectionDefinition gates it only from 2002) and every segment is resident: AlterSwitchEmitter.EmitFields declares each altered GO TO's target as an instance field that EmitAlter assigns and EmitGoTo reads, and nothing resets it across a CALL, so the return from EXIT PROGRAM finds the segment exactly as it was left. The witness ALTERs a GO TO in segment 50, CALLs a program that EXIT PROGRAMs, and prints LAST-USED. Probes (work-slice-70): r1a (segment 60, PERFORM then CALL into a segmented subprogram) LAST-USED; r1b class e (a failed CALL ON EXCEPTION then a good CALL, segment 99) CALL FAILED / LAST-USED; r1c class c (GOBACK, 2002) refused COBOL0880. Classes a, d, f do not reach a control-transfer rule. The complementary INITIAL-state arms are not implemented (r1d: a segment-50 ALTER survives a second PERFORM from segment 0, printing ALTERED where 1985 prints INITIAL): kb/Work PB5084, rows 1985-GR-XVI.1.4.3-1..3, not this rule.

next.reason: 1985: "Control is transferred explicitly to that segment as the result of the execution of an EXIT PROGRAM statement."; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the Segmentation module; the EXIT PROGRAM candidates say nothing about segments or segment state.". No 2023 clause holds the Segmentation feature. The EXIT PROGRAM transfer rules (14.6.3, 14.9.14) never mention segments, so the segment-state requirement is dropped with the module.
